chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who is in Basra and is from the people of Kufa, having a house and residence there, so he passes through Kufa, and he is merely passing through, not intending to stay except for the time it takes to prepare for a day or two days. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He stays in the outskirts of the city and shortens (his prayer).' I said, 'And if he goes to his family?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the complete (prayer).'
ai.seo_question: When does a traveler passing through their home city shorten or complete their prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between a traveler retaining their 'home base' status versus becoming a resident upon visiting family, a key nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding the duration of stay (usually 4 days) that triggers full prayer. It highlights the practical application of the 'city' (Madinah) boundary, where the outskirts are treated as part of the travel domain, ensuring the traveler maintains the concession of Qasr until they effectively re-establish domestic life. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic law in accommodating transient lifestyles while preserving the spiritual discipline of the complete prayer when one is settled.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who happens to be in Al-Basra and he is from the people of Al-Kufa, there being a house for him in it, and a lodging. So he passes by Al-Kufa, and rather he is just passing by, not intending the staying except of a measurement of preparing for a day or two days. Heasws said: ‘He stays in the side of the city and he shortens (the Salāt)’. I said, ‘Supposing he goes over to his family?’ Heasws said: ‘Upon him is the complete (Salāt)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in al-Basra and he is from al- Kufah. He has a house there and he passes by al-Kufah just as a passer-by without an intention to stay there except for picking up supplies within one or two days. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to stay in one side of the city and perform his Salah (prayer) as reduced.’ I then asked, ‘What is he required to do if he visits his family?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to perform his Salah (prayer) complete.’”
